challenge: 07 says the Chariot-first, PayPal-second order 'matches CNV-PAY-007' and recommends 'Keep CNV-PAY-001 and CNV-PAY-007 (Chariot first, PayPal second)'.
evidence: CNV-PAY-007 in clauses/c1_finance_payments.json is 'Bank activity feeds, debit blocks and fee bearers'. It says nothing about partner order. The Chariot/PayPal candidacy comes from SPD-CMP-003 (requirements/discovery/2026-11-24-open-decision-resolution-review.md). CNV-PAY-007 does matter to Chariot in a different way: disbursement accounts may be ACH-debited only by 'explicitly approved rail partners that fund by ACH debit'. That clause bears on Chariot just-in-time funding.
recommended_revision: Remove the CNV-PAY-007 attribution and cite SPD-CMP-003 (open decision) as the basis for partner order. Add the CNV-PAY-007 debit-block approval to the Chariot activation checklist.

challenge: 09's headline 'gap' is that nothing stops an attacker from changing a charity's registry contact before requesting a bank change. 09 says CNV-PLT-011 covers 'donors only' and proposes PROP-SEC-02 to extend it.
evidence: Two owner-ratified round-2 amendments already close most of this. The c11 amendment to CNV-PLT-011 says: 'The post-change hold SHALL also cover bank-detail changes and, for charities, contact and authorised-signatory changes', and defines CAL0-CAL3. The c10 amendment to CNV-PAY-002 requires the callback contact to come from a record verified at least 30 days earlier (sponsor default) or from an independent public source. Under it, 'any contact or signatory change inside that period disqualifies the contact', and charity users must authenticate at CAL3. 08 cites the CAL3 amendment; 09 does not.
recommended_revision: Rewrite the 09 summary bullet and the section 6 table row: the control is ratified (c10/c11). Re-scope PROP-SEC-02 to what is left: poisoning of the IRS-of-record address or phone via Form 8822-B or a new 990, which feeds the postcard and phone claim routes in 02. Add the c10 and c11 amendments to 09's existing-controls list.

challenge: The conflict between CNV-EXP-002 (pay through an existing partner enrolment with no new enrolment) and destination-evidence rules is stated against the wrong clause and is understated.
evidence: The c10 amendment says destination evidence combinations 'SHALL be exactly' either (a) a bank-originated owner match plus cooling-off plus notice on two channels, or (b) a charity document plus a registry-sourced callback plus cooling-off plus notice, with a floor of 1 business day. Chariot verifies the officer's identity and opens a Column DDA 'legally owned by your organization' (Chariot help pages). That is neither (a) nor (b), and Chariot's instant payment conflicts with the cooling-off floor. 09 frames the conflict only against RR-REQ-X-005-r1. None of 02, 07 or 09 cites the 'exactly' amendment.
recommended_revision: Escalate to the owner as CNV-PAY-002 (c10) versus CNV-EXP-002. Propose a third admissible class for owner decision: 'bank-opened account titled to the charity's EIN under the partner bank's CIP/KYB, plus partner-attested control-change events'. Otherwise CNV-EXP-002 cannot be met for Chariot-enrolled charities.

challenge: 05's identity-stress counts (237,858 c3 subordinates; 244,845 c3 organizations sharing a name; 326,159 sharing an address; 2,168 addresses with 10 or more organizations; Toastmasters 6,191; largest group 16,946; c3 rows 1,663,706) are labelled VERIFIED-FACT High. They double-count rows.
evidence: Re-running scripts/reg_source_change_volumes.py bmf-profile on eo1-eo4 gives 237,380 / 235,926 / 317,386 / 2,159 / 6,143 / 16,914 / 1,659,108. Adding eo_pr and eo_xx reproduces 05's figures exactly, with 'eins_on_multiple_rows': 5060: the 5,060 eo_pr/eo_xx rows duplicate eo1-eo4 rows. 04 and 02 use the deduplicated 237,380 and 1,659,108, so the drafts disagree with each other. The shared-name count is also inflated, because a duplicated EIN matches its own name.
recommended_revision: Deduplicate by EIN in profile_bmf (or read only eo1-eo4), re-run, and replace the 05 figures and the REG-010 excerpt. Add a duplicate-EIN guard to the script.

challenge: The number of Pub 78 EINs whose latest auto-revocation row has no reinstatement date differs across drafts: 19,699 in 04, 19,695 in 05; ADVA's re-derivation gives 19,689. The 31,616 BMF figure reproduces.
evidence: Independent script (advA/verify.py): 31,616 still on the BMF, 19,689 also in Pub 78. The differences presumably come from how each script picks the 'latest' row when revocation dates tie; this was not traced.
recommended_revision: Use one script and one tie-break rule (latest posting date, then latest revocation date). Cite a single figure in 04, 05 and 06.

challenge: 04 explains the 31,616 'revoked, not reinstated, still on BMF' EINs as either an incomplete reinstatement field or re-recognition under a new determination (INFERENCE Medium). It does not test which.
evidence: ADVA heuristic: for 22,404 of the 31,616 (71%), the BMF RULING month is later than the latest revocation date. That points mainly to re-recognition under a new determination. Rev. Proc. 2018-32 s4.06 allows reliance on a subsequent listing posted after the auto-revocation posting.
recommended_revision: Add the RULING-after-revocation split. Apply the deterministic s4.06 rule (listing posted after revocation posting means reliance) to that group, and send only the remaining ~9,200 to review.

challenge: The economic model and the enrolment-growth model assume very different partner pre-enrolment. ECO's partner_coverage is 0.30/0.50/0.70 of recipients 'anchored on Fidelity's 67% electronic grant share'. The PAY growth model assumes 2-20% with one partner and 5-45% with two, which yields 8-21% of grants at go-live.
evidence: The Fidelity anchor is invalid for CNV-EXP-002. Fidelity's EFT enrolments are Fidelity-proprietary (Stripe/ACH form, 'queue may take several weeks'), so they are not a supported networked partner whose enrolment Unbound can reuse. ECO's check_share_target of 10% is also inconsistent with 08's planning path: at p=0.10, reaching 67% of grants electronic takes 23-65 months. ECO itself says the direct-enrolment bill 'roughly doubles' at lower coverage.
recommended_revision: Re-run ECO with partner_coverage taken from the scripts/pay_enrollment_growth_model.py tiers (central about 0.10-0.20) and check_share_target from 08's p=0.10 trajectory. Restate the cost-per-grant figures ($2.29 to $1.80) as conditional on the conversion rate achieved.

challenge: 08 calibrates per-invitation conversion to about p<=0.10 from Fidelity's 67% and tells readers to plan on p=0.10. It does not weigh contrary vendor evidence from forced-claim designs, which 03 itself reports: Chariot 94.57% of payments electronic; TIFIN 82% of dollars electronic in its first 4 months.
evidence: Fidelity's channel is an opt-in form with a multi-week queue and no hold (Fidelity FAQ). Chariot holds each grant for 5 business days for claim. One p conflates mechanisms with very different friction. Both Chariot figures are VENDOR-CLAIM with undisclosed bases, so neither direction is established.
recommended_revision: Model conversion by mechanism (opt-in form, hold-and-claim, owner-match with zero charity effort). Cite the Chariot and TIFIN vendor figures as an upper bound, and keep p=0.10 as the conservative case.

challenge: Is Ren's network more defensible than 02 assumes? 02 places Ren's defensible asset in the verified-payee layer. The repo attrition census places Ren's stickiness in sponsor-side platform integration, inside exactly Unbound's entry segment (CNV-ECO-004).
evidence: From research/mission-2026-11-14/queue-ren-iphi-attrition.md: 6 of 57 iPhi sponsors left in 2023-2026. 5 of the 6 were community foundations, which are not Unbound's entry segment. Only 1 of 26 faith/affinity/national sponsors left. NPT, J.P. Morgan and ICGF moved deeper into Ren (GivingPoint). Every exit went to Foundant or akoyaGO; none went to a new entrant. JCF kept paying Ren after switching (repo ONB note). No evidence of a charity-side network effect was found (Ren publishes no claimed-profile or verified-payee counts).
recommended_revision: Add a section on sponsor-side lock-in (admin, accounting, portal, white-label and contract terms) and rank the payee layer second. State that national/advisor-distributed churn away from Ren is near zero in the public evidence. This raises the bar CNV-ECO-004 must clear.

challenge: 02 says 'Ren's 1.8M+ is therefore not proprietary coverage. VERIFIED-FACT, High.'
evidence: The IRS counts reproduce exactly: 1,984,891; 1,659,108; 1,715,430; Pub 78 1,437,288; 997. But a matching size is not evidence of provenance. 02's own section 2 grades the IRS-origin claim INFERENCE Medium-High and notes that Candid's counts are the same size.
recommended_revision: Split the claim: the counts are VERIFIED-FACT; 'not proprietary' is INFERENCE, Medium-High.

challenge: 02 reads the TY2024 Schedule I recipients absent from the 2026-11 BMF (about 7%) and from Pub 78 (16%) as a tail 'outside the IRS files'.
evidence: The comparison has a time skew: TY2024 grantees are matched to a BMF two years later, so organizations revoked or terminated after the grant count as 'outside'. The Pub 78 gap also includes subordinates and churches that are legitimately absent (Pub 78 lists 0 of 237,380 c3 subordinates). 06 estimates revocation incidence among grantees at about 0.3% a year.
recommended_revision: Match against a contemporaneous BMF snapshot (NCCS mirror) and split the gap into subordinate, church, revoked after the grant, government/foreign, and true unknown.

challenge: Does Chariot create an unacceptable dependency? 07 recommends Chariot first and rates sponsor lock-in 'medium'. It covers channel conflict but leaves out competitor alignment, change of control and deposit-insurance limits.
evidence: Chariot Disbursements partners include direct competitors: Daffy, Endaoment and four other DAF providers (Chariot post); TIFIN Give (release dated 2025-12-02). Chariot is VC-backed (an $11M Series A in 2024 per press). Chariot Deposit Accounts are Column N.A. DDAs, FDIC-insured to $250,000 per depositor. Sponsor funds in transit above that are uninsured, and both legs sit at one bank. Mitigant verified: the charity's Chariot DDA is legally owned by the charity, with its own account and routing number, so it survives a Chariot change of control and can receive sponsor-originated ACH (07 rule R5).
recommended_revision: Add to the activation checklist: a change-of-control termination right; export of enrolment status and control-change events; a per-partner exposure cap no higher than the insured amount or a sponsor-accepted uninsured limit (CNV-PLT-012); and the PayPal (or second-rail) adapter before scale, not after. Keep Chariot-first for Release 1.

challenge: Does shared verification add systemic risk that outweighs its benefit? 09 bounds the risk with five controls. It does not size the benefit, assign losses, or deal with the knowledge-imputation and cross-tenant effects of the controls.
evidence: Benefit is small. ECO prices first verification at $1.35 and instant verification at $1.50-4.00 per enrolment. A bank-originated owner match costs the charity no effort, so re-verifying per sponsor is cheap; sharing mainly helps charities with no owner-match data. Cost: correlated exposure (09's own model), unallocated loss when sponsor B relies on evidence A collected, and a velocity tripwire that pauses every sponsor based on other tenants' activity (cross-tenant signal; CNV-TEN-001). Rev. Proc. 2018-32 s4.04(3) and s5.02(2) remove reliance if a grantor 'was aware of' the deficiencies. Shared flags could widen awareness, a point 06 covers only for public facts.
recommended_revision: Release 1: share control and claim evidence and public facts only. Keep destination (bank) evidence sponsor-scoped, with per-sponsor owner-match re-verification. Make shared destination evidence a later option, gated on a measured friction benefit, a written loss-allocation term, and counsel's view on s4.04/s5.02 imputation.

challenge: Does the independent registry distract from the core, and would buying Candid be cheaper or safer? 05 recommends a first-party registry with no build-versus-buy comparison.
evidence: ECO sizes registry setup at about $319k ($113k-$1.07M) plus about $75k a year. Candid API list prices start at $2,750 a year (VENDOR-CLAIM; platform/resale licence price unknown). But Candid Charity Check monitors the same IRS and OFAC files (Candid FAQ) and still cites the superseded Rev. Proc. 2011-33. Rev. Proc. 2018-32 s8.01 lets any third party, Unbound included, issue a reliance report from BMF data. Candid does not solve subordinate rosters (s6.03), non-BMF recipients or payee verification, and its terms restrict AI/ML use and require deletion on termination. Sponsor policies do name GuideStar (Alaska CF, CF of Northern Nevada; NPT points donors to GuideStar), so expectation and auditor friction is real.
recommended_revision: Add an explicit build/buy/hybrid table to 05. Keep UNB-CHAR-DEC-001. Evaluate a non-runtime Candid cross-check (reconciliation QA, not a decision input) only if the licence permits; run auditor interviews on acceptance of an Unbound s8.01 report.

challenge: Do the proposed capabilities already exist among competitors? 08's 'Where Unbound can differ' (no charity software use, one authorisation for many sponsors, partner-neutral routing) presents parity features as differentiators.
evidence: 'Claim a Chariot Account one time to receive these payments ... from all Chariot Disbursement partners' (TIFIN/Chariot release). Ren says 'validated once, trusted across the entire platform'. Fidelity ACH pays the charity's own bank with no portal (Fidelity FAQ). CAF America reuses validation for 1-3 years. Candid pushes revocations in under 24h. Only versioned, provenance-bound decisions and sponsor-portable evidence remain undocumented elsewhere, and 03 correctly rates that a HYPOTHESIS.
recommended_revision: Relabel 08's items as parity-plus. State the residual differentiator as sponsor-held, rail-neutral, re-verifiable evidence plus deterministic decision replay, and test it with sponsors before ranking it as an advantage.

challenge: Is public charity data insufficient for reliable vetting? (challenge 2)
evidence: The drafts' limits match the primary law verbatim: s4.02 (posting-date protection), s4.04 (knowledge exception), s4.06 (subsequent listing), s6.01 (names), s6.02 (not before listing), s6.03 (no reliance for subordinates) and s8.01 (third-party report fields), checked against rp-18-32.pdf. Measured gaps reproduce: Pub 78 lists 0 of 237,380 subordinates; 2026 posting lag p50 is 88 days (39,415 of 53,120 postings at exactly 88); 2025 p50 is 89; the August batches are 40,453 (2025) and 38,826 (2026); 122,787 of 184,830 reinstatements are retroactive; 57,583 990-N rows carry the terminated flag. The drafts already say public data establishes status but not existence, subordinate inclusion, government EINs or bank ownership.
recommended_revision: None beyond ADVA-04/05/06. Note in 04 that the 88-day median is a batch artefact of the August posting, not a continuous lag.

challenge: Nacha 2026 rule dates and the False Pretenses definition as cited.
evidence: Nacha's Phase 2 page gives June 19, 2026, with a practical date of Monday, June 22, 2026, for all other non-consumer Originators, TPSPs and TPSs. The definition includes misrepresenting 'the ownership of an account to be credited'. Phase 1 was March 20, 2026, for parties with 6M+ originations in 2023. The drafts are accurate. Whether the rule applies to Unbound is still counsel's question; CNV-PAY-001 already accepts TPSP obligations by contract.
recommended_revision: Optionally add the Phase 1 date and threshold for completeness.

challenge: Vanguard '66,785 unique charities CY2025' is cited to CMP-026 and the repo grant-count CSV. Neither contains the figure.
evidence: The CMP-026 excerpt gives '130,000+ ... since inception'. The repo CSV has grant counts only. Press coverage reports 'nearly 67,000 nonprofits' for 2025, so the number is plausible but uncited. The primary Vanguard release was not fetched.
recommended_revision: Cite the primary Vanguard 2025 release, or state 'nearly 67,000 (press)'.

challenge: Self-reported sponsor and vendor counts are classed VERIFIED-FACT (for example CMP-005 Fidelity '227,000'; CMP-026). 09 says no top-20 sponsor publishes a callback before a charity bank change.
evidence: Fidelity's FAQ confirms 'nearly 227,000 charitable organizations', but it is a first-party self-report. The same FAQ says Fidelity 'may call your organization's publicly available phone number to verify banking and/or contact information'. That is a discretionary callback, so 09's 'mandatory' qualifier is technically true but leaves out comparable practice.
recommended_revision: Reclass self-reported counts as VENDOR-CLAIM (first-party, High that the statement exists). Add Fidelity's discretionary callback to 09.

challenge: Scope and focus. Track A proposes a large new requirement surface for a product still in the requirements phase: 05 (11 new requirements plus 6 shared stores), 06 (a state model), 08 (an enrolment loop), 09 (PROP-SEC-01..15). 20's own economics says moving from check to e-pay saves about $1.07 a grant, that the network is a 'sales/switching asset not margin lever', and that migration is on the Release 1 critical path.
evidence: INFERENCE from 20-economic-analysis.md and the ONB tension note (Release 1 has no migration, yet CNV-ECO-004 targets existing sponsors). No draft splits its proposals into a Release 1 minimum and later work.
recommended_revision: Tier the Track A proposals. Release 1 minimum: IRS and OFAC ingestion, subordinate and church rules, destination evidence per c10, the Chariot adapter, and sponsor-ACH fallback. Defer: the open dataset, shared destination evidence, the growth loop beyond codes on checks, and the commercial-data options.
